votes.evidence: The facts in the finding are accurate. products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125 `has_reviewable_repo_config` returns `.exists()` over the team's synced, enabled configs for any repository. products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:72-81 exposes that value as `stamphog_connected`. products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1133-1147 then filters on `repository__iexact=repository` and returns quietly, logging `stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable`, when no config covers the PR's repository. products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1066 uses `stamphog_connected` only to disable a switch that is still off.
votes.refutation: This is how the code is meant to work, and it is documented; it is not a defect. The switch is a per-user preference for future Inbox PRs. When the user flips it, those PRs don't exist yet, so there is no repository to check. A per-repository check cannot be done at that point. The flag's own help_text (settings.py:50-54) says it means "at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository". It only decides whether the switch has anything to act on at all. The `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` help_text (settings.py:27-33) says the review "only takes effect when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository". The task docstring (tasks.py:1122-1123) calls the per-repository skip an intentional, self-scoping no-op. The skip is logged, so it is observable. For repositories that are covered, the switch does what it says. The suggested fix is to guess which repositories self-driving tasks will target, which is a product and UX improvement rather than a correctness bug. The earlier validator on this finding also marked it is_valid=false.

votes.evidence:
The code does what the finding describes. products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125 `has_reviewable_repo_config` returns `.exists()` over the whole team. products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1135-1149 filters on `repository__iexact=repository` and returns quietly, logging `stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable`, when no config covers the PR's repo. But the team-wide check is on purpose and documented, not a hidden mismatch:
- products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:50-53: the help text defines stamphog_connected as "at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository". Its only job is to disable the switch when Stamphog is not set up at all.
- products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:27-32: the toggle help text says it "only takes effect when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository".
- products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_settings_api.py:60-75 (`test_stamphog_connected_requires_a_synced_enabled_repo_config`) pins that team-level contract.
- products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:137-141 and tasks.py:1123-1124 describe the per-repo no-op as by design: it scopes itself to repos where the Stamphog App is installed.
- products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1062-1068: the UI uses the flag only as a "not set up yet" gate.
votes.refutation:
The toggle is a per-user preference that covers all future Inbox PRs. It works correctly for every repo connected to Stamphog. Stamphog can't review a repo where its GitHub App isn't installed, and that follows from the product setup, not from a bug in this code. The flag's contract (at least one connected repo, used only to disable the switch when nothing is set up) is stated in the serializer help text and locked in by test_settings_api.py:60-75.

A per-repo check would not fit a settings switch anyway. The switch applies to PRs that don't exist yet, whose repos can't be known ahead of time, and the "silent" skip is an intended info log. At most this is a wording tweak to the switch description, which is a UX preference and not a defect. Nothing is lost that the user could reasonably have expected: a repo that isn't connected was never going to be reviewed.

votes.evidence:
Reachability: the trigger can happen in production. products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125 `has_reviewable_repo_config` returns true when the team has any synced, enabled config (`.exists()`, no repository filter). products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:73-82 exposes that as `stamphog_connected`. products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1133-1146 filters by `repository__iexact=repository` and returns with only `logger.info("stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable")` when no config matches. So a team with Stamphog on repo X and Inbox PRs on repo Y can turn the switch on and get no Stamphog review for Y. That part of the finding matches the code.

Why this is not a defect: the coarse, team-wide check is a documented design choice, not an accident. settings.py:50-54 says in its help_text that `stamphog_connected` means "at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository". settings.py:28-32 says the toggle "Only takes effect when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository". tasks.py:1122-1123 describes the per-repository no-op as intentional self-scoping. The flag only decides whether to disable the switch when nothing is connected at all (CodeReviewScene.tsx:1063-1068). It never promises that every repository is covered.

The switch is opt-in and changes nothing else. Nothing is lost or wrongly approved. Stamphog just does not run on repositories where its GitHub App is not set up, which is how per-repository GitHub App installs normally work, and the user connected those repositories themselves. At most the switch description (CodeReviewScene.tsx:1054-1057) could mention that it only covers repositories connected to Stamphog. That is a copy/UX preference, and the suggested fix of computing coverage per target repository is speculative scope creep. The original validator also marked this finding invalid.
votes.refutation: The mismatch can happen, but the code and its docs mean it on purpose. `stamphog_connected` is documented as "at least one synced, enabled repository" (settings.py:50-54). Per-repository self-scoping is the documented behavior of process_inbox_pr_review (tasks.py:1122-1123, 1144-1146). The flag's only job is to disable the switch when Stamphog is not set up at all (CodeReviewScene.tsx:1063-1068). An opt-in switch that has no effect on repositories the user never connected to Stamphog is expected GitHub App scoping, not a correctness defect. What remains is a copy tweak, which is a style/UX preference.
